surface_mechanism_description: The ALD process involved alternating exposures to diethyl zinc/H2O at 177 °C, with a nucleation layer of amorphous Al2O3 deposited prior to ZnO. The reactor was evacuated and purged with Ar between exposures.
evidence: Prior to ZnO deposition, an ,0.26-nm-thick nucleation layer of amorphous Al2O3 was deposited in two cycles of trimethyl aluminum/H2O at the same conditions as ZnO. The purpose of such an Al2O3 nucleation layer was to prepare a densely hydroxylated surface to minimize any nucleation delay of the subsequent ALD of ZnO.
